options.content:
Showing Kubernetes usage for **${__user.login}**, broken out per project.

This is a **default view, not enforced isolation** — it filters by the account you signed in with. It is not a security boundary: Grafana's Explore and query API remain available and are not scoped by this filter. A project counts as yours while it still has a Deployment: deleting a project removes that, so it drops out here even though its namespace is kept. Kubernetes and Nomad usage are both shown, each broken out per project.

panels.title: Your projects
panels.description: Projects with a running workload on EITHER platform. Derived from the same series the CPU graphs use, so this count cannot disagree with the graphs beside it. Counting Kubernetes Deployments alone missed Nomad-only projects entirely. A project counts while its workload EXISTS, even if it is still building or unhealthy, so a freshly submitted project is never shown as zero.

targets.expr:
count(
  (
      sum by (namespace) (
        rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{container!="",container!="POD"}[5m])
      )
    or
      sum by (namespace) (nomad_client_allocs_cpu_total_percent)
    or
      sum by (namespace) (kube_deployment_created)
    or
      sum by (namespace) (nomad_nomad_job_summary_running)
  )
  * on (namespace) group_left(label_project)
    kube_namespace_labels{label_owner="${__user.login}"}
) or vector(0)

panels.title: CPU by project
panels.description: Container CPU, summed per project. Sourced from cAdvisor, joined to the namespace's owner label via kube_namespace_labels.

defaults.noValue: No projects yet. Create one from the portal and it will appear here.

panels.title: Memory by project
panels.description: Container working-set memory, summed per project.

defaults.noValue: No projects yet. Create one from the portal and it will appear here.

panels.title: Your projects, right now
panels.description: One row per project with a running workload, Kubernetes or Nomad. Same source as the graphs. A project counts while its workload EXISTS, even if it is still building or unhealthy, so a freshly submitted project is never shown as zero.

targets.expr:
count by (label_project) (
  (
      sum by (namespace) (
        rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{container!="",container!="POD"}[5m])
      )
    or
      sum by (namespace) (nomad_client_allocs_cpu_total_percent)
    or
      sum by (namespace) (kube_deployment_created)
    or
      sum by (namespace) (nomad_nomad_job_summary_running)
  )
  * on (namespace) group_left(label_project)
    kube_namespace_labels{label_owner="${__user.login}"}
)

panels.title: Nomad CPU by project
panels.description: Nomad allocation CPU, summed per project. Joined to the owner label on the NAMESPACE: the Nomad namespace and the Kubernetes namespace are the same string (tenant-PROJECT), which is the only identity a Nomad allocation carries - the job ID is the constant 'starter' and there is no Meta block.

defaults.noValue: Nothing running on Nomad. Projects deployed to Kubernetes appear above.

panels.title: Nomad memory by project
panels.description: Nomad allocation RSS, summed per project. Same namespace join as the CPU panel.

defaults.noValue: Nothing running on Nomad. Projects deployed to Kubernetes appear above.
